coverage_explanation: Tests exercise repeated mechanical-fault inputs, both sides of the calibrated current and temperature thresholds, fan operation independent of mechanical-fault priority, repeated fault-code reporting on separate fault entries, visible LED alarm activity, and phase-independent aspects of the rotating display. Display checks cover rotation, repetition after a complete three-page cycle, and states in which all three displayed numbers must coincide. Coverage is partial: the supported checks cannot reliably witness an unspecified audible cadence over a time interval, so audible alarm operation is not asserted. The suite also does not completely identify each display page independently of its unspecified initial phase, and therefore does not fully verify overload/overheat status numbers, their priority, or numerical calibration across the complete display range. Current-threshold discrimination is exercised but is not independently established by the fan checks.
assumptions: The disclosed bench defaults apply: D13 is an active-HIGH LED connected through a resistor to GND.
The vibration switch on D2 uses the disclosed GND-switch electrical semantics: INPUT_PULLUP, released HIGH, active LOW. Released levels are injected explicitly.
Current and LM35 temperature use the supplied ADC calibrations, not host temperature-input injection.
The initial TM1637 page is unspecified. Rotation checks compare observations separated by the specified two-second page period without requiring a particular first page.
The selected display-calibration points produce the same integer under ordinary truncation or nearest-integer rounding. Other integer-conversion boundaries remain uncovered.
No alarm frequency, audible cadence, LED blink cadence, normal-state serial message, or fault-message label is imposed. LED alarm checks require only an observed illuminated state during each fault.

The reference chooses a continuous 1000 Hz fault tone, a steady fault LED, fault reporting on entry, and current as the initial display page. These are reference implementation choices, not additional candidate requirements.
